reasoning: The claimed damage holds, and it is only a LOW-severity local DoS. AnthropicWireTypes.swift:71 accepts any finite Double as utilization. toSnapshot (AnthropicWireTypes.swift:140-150, 164-170, 176-190) and UsageWindow.init (UsageWindow.swift:15-23) pass it through without a finiteness or range clamp. VendorSnapshot.maxUtilization (UsageSnapshot.swift:70-72) and UsageStore.swift:378-380 carry the value into the menu-bar label. That label's mode is the default: AppConfig.swift:230 sets menuBarMode = .iconAndPercent, and the card is open by default. MenuBarLabelView.swift:41 then runs Int(percent.rounded()), and Swift's Int(Double) aborts the process (it does not throw) when the value is outside Int's range, e.g. 1e300. The same unchecked conversion appears at PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:97/100/110 and NotificationService.swift:102. I found no clamp anywhere between the source and these conversions. A crash kills the whole process, so monitoring stops for every vendor, not just Anthropic. The cached payload is decoded again on relaunch within the TTL or as a stale fallback, which supports the crash-loop claim. Limits: the attacker has to be Anthropic itself or a compromised api.anthropic.com. Ordinary network interception is ruled out by TLS. Nothing is exposed and nothing is written. The harm is availability of a desktop monitor only, which fits the LOW rating.
